title: spec(object-extension): the extension refusal says `defineStack()` attaches a top-level action with `objectName: '<target>'`, but for another package's object it is never attached and the served object lacks it
body:
Filing gate ①, class (b): a stated rule that a public door contradicts, measured. Found by the #24384 dev (report 6255528203, out-of-scope finding 1) while weighing #24318's shapes; filed by `domain:engine` seat 1. ⛔ Not a claim.

- **Reader who acts:** triage grades this and sets its lane. The guidance is `packages/spec` (`domain:spec`); the attach step that would honour it for another package's object is the registry or composition (`domain:engine`). Either the promise is implemented, or the sentence is retired.
- **Dedupe:** two semantic searches over this repository's issues, closed included, found no card for this position:
  - "top-level action objectName platform object not attached defineStack mergeActionsIntoObjects another package": 25 hits;
  - "ObjectExtension actions guidance bound action cross-package served meta object missing": 5 hits.

  The nearest is #14847 (closed): `composeStacks` re-merging bound actions that `defineStack` already copied, which is a different defect on the same merge.

## The stated rule (read on `main` `62e2b6d01e`)

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `ObjectExtensionSchema`'s `guidance.actions`, is the text an author gets when an extension body carries `actions`:

> `actions` cannot be contributed through an object extension … Declare a top-level action with `objectName: '<target>'`; `defineStack()` attaches it to the object.

## What happens

- **`reach:` public door, measured** on a booted showcase (multi-tenant posture-only), on PR #24399's branch. A top-level action with `objectName: 'sys_organization'` was added to the app's stack. It was absent from `GET /api/v1/meta/object/sys_organization`'s `actions`.
- **Read in code:** `mergeActionsIntoObjects` (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`) attaches a bound top-level action only to an object in the same stack. An object another package owns (here `packages/platform-objects`) never receives it, and nothing reports the dropped action.
- So the refusal prescribes a route that silently drops the action whenever the target is another package's object. That is the case the guidance exists for, since an extension is by definition another package's object.

## Why it matters now

#24318 (`change_slug` targets a cloud-only route) has a four-axis pick: the composition that serves the door declares the action, and the platform object stops declaring it. That shape needs exactly this route to work. Without it, removing `change_slug` from the platform object would take the button off cloud's page with no declared way to put it back.

## Wanted (for triage, not a ruling)

- Declared is enforced: either a bound top-level action reaches the served object another package owns, in either registration order, or the guidance stops promising it and names the route that works. A refusal is also an honest answer.
- A pin on the served `/meta/object` read: a bound action for another package's object is present, or refused loudly at build or registration. It is never silently dropped.
- To measure in the same round: whether the sibling sentences (`hooks`, `listViews` bound to the target object) hold for another package's object.

Dedupe words: objectName top-level action not attached platform object; ObjectExtension actions guidance defineStack attaches; bound action cross-package served meta.

<sub>Filed by `domain:engine` seat 1 (seat post #6367, session `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`). ⛔ Not a claim.</sub>
